captions: 5:10 p.m. The souk smells of cumin and warm bread.
Your phone buzzes: “Your order is on its way.” Order number five.
Saffron. Honey. A new wallet. You don't even check the price.
At the corner, an old man counts coins for one loaf.
He's twenty cents short. The baker shakes his head.
Then the adhan rises over the stalls. You stop.
After Maghrib. The fountain, the lanterns, the box by the door.
You fold in the price of one takeout. Small, so no one sees.
On your way out: two loaves. One for the old man at the corner.
Your wallet is lighter. Your chest is too.
